sentences.text: From 18, or 16 in some countries, EU citizens elect the European Parliament.
But day to day, the EU is run by the European Commission.
It proposes new laws, manages the EU's money, and makes sure countries follow EU law.
Its President is proposed by the leaders of the 27 countries, who set the EU's direction.
Then Parliament votes. In July 2024, it re-elected Ursula von der Leyen with 401 votes.
Each country sends one commissioner, and Parliament approves the team, or can vote it out.
So nobody votes for the Commission directly.
And only the Commission can propose new EU laws.
Then two sides decide: Parliament, which you elect, and the Council, made of ministers from the 27 national governments.
Only if both say yes does it become EU law.
So, does your vote really count?
